metadata.title: 1920s Chinese Strike Causal Knowledge Graph
metadata.description: Visual representation of 16 dispersed words from 1920s newspaper press before clustering.

A.name: Economic Grievances & Inflation
A.description: Post-WWI economic depression, soaring rice prices, currency volatility, and unlivable wages.

B.name: Labor Organizing & Solidarity
B.description: Establishment of labor syndicates, strike committees, boycott manifestos, and picket enforcement.

C.name: Strike Action & Work Stoppage
C.description: Mass walkouts, dock shutdowns, street demonstrations, and systemic withdrawal of labor.
C.causal_role: Central Strike Event (A, B -> C -> D)

D.name: Economic Paralysis & Colonial Impact
D.description: Harbor standstill, stranded steamships, supply shortages, and imperial legislative negotiations.

nodes.context: Stagnant daily laborer wages amidst sharp post-war currency fluctuations.
Skyrocketing price of staple rice threatening subsistence of dock families.
Exhausting operational hours demanded from maritime and transport coolies.
General cost-of-living index surges driving desperate economic petitions.
The central maritime guild led by Su Zhaozheng organizing across Hong Kong and Canton.
Executive coordinating council managing strike logistics, food rations, and strategy.
Organized worker patrols enforcing the anti-colonial shipping embargo.
Leaflets distributed across treaty ports calling for national anti-imperial unity.
Complete stoppage of maritime and municipal work paralyzing the colony.
Stevedores and cargo loaders abandoning British ships in Victoria Harbour.
Sympathy strikes spreading to domestic servants, tram drivers, and clerks.
Gatherings of thousands marching through urban centers demanding rights and dignity.
Over 150 merchant vessels anchored idle with zero cargo discharge capacity.
Complete standstill of coastal and trans-Pacific commercial steamer traffic.
Retail closures, supply shortages, and emergency rationing across Victoria.
Colonial government and shipping conglomerates agreeing to wage hikes and union recognition.
